answer: Each round, the protocol draws a fresh jury from the identity registry, so a sybil cluster cannot predict or pre-bribe its graders. Grading is like light through a prism: one submission splits into independent, randomly assigned verdicts. An attacker who controls many fake identities gains little, because controlling one jury seat says nothing about the next draw, and repeated exposure lets honest reviewers mark the timber of a cluster's behavior across rounds. Reputation accrues per identity, yet no single grove of colluders can capture the aggregate. Failure mode to watch: registry.
